newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - July 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - July 15.

text.p: Following are the highlights of Irish press on Tuesday:
- The bulk of money in Ansbacher deposits moved shortly after start of the Dunnes/Haughey tribunal.
- Breakthrough in Cork murder enquiry into death of Sophie Toscan du Plantier as police believe alibi of main suspect can now be undermined
- New difficulties for government as punt nears ERM ceiling level
- Unionists say credibility of British government damaged
- Memories of the bad old days of the 1993 currency crisis are revived
- Arcon to focus on its core mining business in future
- Investors at troubled Mackie back emergency rights issue
- Market bubbling up on back of buoyancy in British trading - Greencore takes over Kears

- All eyes on Dublin Castle as Charlie Haughey takes the stand - Senior IRA figures likely to be prosecuted for McCabe murder - Momentum grows to revalue punt as tensions rise in ERM - Corporate rescue mission needed after two years of turmoil at CIE
- Ben Dunne insisted he neither sought nor received favour from former prime minister Charles Haughey in return for 1.3 million Irish pound donation.
- Experts claims 'black' econony is 4.0 billion punts - Manchester United chairman Martin Edwards and family interest have realised almost 6.0 million sterling selling shares in the league champions
